families.name: _YOUTUBE_VIDEO_ID_RE, _SAFE_ID_RE, _CORRELATION_ID_RE, _ISO_DATE_RE, _SAFE_PATH_RE, _EMAIL_RE (lines 28-43)
families.purpose: Validate ids, dates, paths and emails at input boundaries.
hazards: Anchored with ^...$ but re.match and $ accept a trailing newline: _EMAIL_RE and _ISO_DATE_RE return True for 'a@b.co\n' and '2026-11-15T10:00:00+05:30\n'. Use fullmatch or \Z.
_CORRELATION_ID_RE is also defined in sanitization.py.
families.notes_for_row: Not checked against tests/ in this sweep.

families.name: _SESSION_ID_RE, _CORRELATION_ID_RE, _USER_INPUT_CONTROL_RE, _USER_INPUT_SCRIPT_RE, _URL_CREDENTIALS_RE (lines 13-19, 117)
families.purpose: Strip control characters and script tags from user input; redact URL credentials; validate session and correlation ids.
hazards: Same $-newline acceptance as security_utils for the id validators.
_URL_CREDENTIALS_RE replaces the whole match including scheme when a bare replacement string is used; only a \1 backreference preserves the scheme (regex-only probe, call site not read).

families.name: Span-attribute allowlist (lines 179-183) and secret scrubbers _SENTINEL_REGEX, _AUTH_HEADER_REGEX, _TOKEN_PARAM_REGEX, _KEY_PATTERN_REGEX (lines 278-284)
families.purpose: Keep only allowlisted telemetry attributes; redact bearer/basic auth headers, token query params and key-shaped strings before logs or traces leave the process.
hazards: .*_(tokens|ms|...)$ attribute allowlist is unanchored at the start and admits any suffix match.
_SENTINEL_REGEX sentinel[_\-\w]* is broad and can redact unrelated identifiers containing 'sentinel'.

families.name: Secret-shape patterns (lines 26-31)
families.purpose: Redact sk-, ghp_, JWT, Bearer, PEM private-key headers and password assignments from manifest output.
hazards: Secret shapes duplicated in observability and sanitization (hypothesis: not diffed in this sweep). Keep one list and import it.

families.name: EMAIL_REGEX, PHONE_REGEX, ID_REGEX (lines 205-209) and _REFUSAL_PATTERN (line 29)
families.purpose: Scrub PII from telemetry rows before insert; classify refusals.
hazards: ID_REGEX matches any grouped 12-digit number, so non-personal reference ids are redacted (over-redaction, low severity).
PHONE_REGEX matches any 10-digit run including numeric ids.

families.name: PIIScanner.EMAIL/PHONE/AADHAAR/SSN/IP/URL_QUERY_PARAM regexes (lines 8-13)
families.purpose: Detect and redact PII (email, phone, Aadhaar-style id, SSN, IP, URL query values).
hazards: AADHAAR_REGEX matches any grouped 12-digit number (probe: 'ref 1234 5678 9012' matches), so it over-redacts. Probe confirmed.
SSN_REGEX is correct on the probe cases: '123-45-6789' matches, '000-12-3456' does not.

families.name: GREETING_RE, GREETING_VOCATIVE_RE, GREETING_SEQUENCE_RE, CONVERSATIONAL_OPENER_RE (lines 7-50)
families.purpose: Deterministic greeting short-circuit for pure greetings with a closed vocative vocabulary.
hazards: Closed vocative list is good: probe shows 'namaste suicide' and 'hi kms' are rejected by is_deterministic_greeting (correct), 'hello there' and 'Namaste! Good morning.' are accepted (correct).
Regex is a closed-vocabulary check; the list could live as data (move_to_lexicon_data is optional).
families.notes_for_row: Comments cite a 2026-10-23 live run; test files not checked.

families.name: _TIER2_GREETING_RE, _TIER2_STACKED_RE, _TIER2_OPENER_RE, _TIER3_HELP_RE, _TIER4_GLOSSARY_RE (lines 36-124)
families.purpose: Second greeting and help grammar that short-circuits to canned replies.
hazards: CLAUDE.md lists app/intake/short_circuit.py as a second greeting grammar and dormant (no call site). The caller grep was not run in this sweep, so this is a hypothesis until confirmed.
If it is live, its vocative list (_VOCATIVES) differs from routing_primitives, so the same input can classify differently.

families.name: GREETINGS_RE (line 27)
families.purpose: Pre-route compact greetings to CASUAL before the LLM classifier.
hazards: Trailing (\s+.*)?$ accepts any suffix: GREETINGS_RE.match('hi there suicide') is truthy. preroute_intent avoids a crisis mis-route only because DISTRESS_RE runs first. This is ordering-dependent safety.
Open vocabulary, unlike routing_primitives (closed vocatives).

families.name: DISTRESS_RE (line 34), used by preroute_intent (line 95)
families.purpose: Acute distress keyword gate before LLM classification; the call site is rag/nodes/intent.py:525, inside the graph after the Distress stage.
hazards: Confirmed false negatives: 'I am feeling suicidal' (no match), 'hi I am suicidal' (preroute returns CASUAL), 'I have panic attacks' (no match: attacks is not matched because the pattern ends with \battack\b).
No stemming, so suicidal/suicides and attacks are missed. Owned by the crisis work already tracked as A12. Any fix must be measured with the human-written crisis set, not this sweep.
families.notes_for_row: already_registered=A12 (docs/plans/PROD_READINESS_TASK_LIST_2026-10-11.md, A12 crisis regex does not converge).

families.name: MEDITATION_RE (line 75)
families.purpose: Route imperative meditation requests to MEDITATION, requiring an imperative verb plus a meditation noun within 40 chars.
hazards: Probe: 'start meditation' matches, 'what is soul sync' does not (both correct). The conservative design is intentional and documented in the file.
It is still a regex judgment of intent; the LLM path is the fallback.

families.name: _THINK_RE, _FENCE_RE, _NUMBERED_RE (lines 27, 28, 47)
families.purpose: Strip reasoning tags and code fences from LLM verdict output, then parse numbered verdicts.
hazards: _THINK_RE is lazy with DOTALL: an unterminated <think> block is left intact and would reach the parser (hypothesis, not probed).
Parsing LLM output with regex is fragile when the model drifts format; verdict failures should abstain, not default to a value (hypothesis: call sites not read).

families.name: _PATTERNS tuple: instruction_override, role_marker, and others (lines 28-58)
families.purpose: Heuristic prompt-injection screen on user and retrieved text.
hazards: Regex screen is a heuristic. Paraphrased overrides ('disregard the rules above') bypass exact phrase lists. Treat as a tripwire, not a guarantee (hypothesis: bypass cases not probed).
Unicode normalisation runs before matching (line 2 imports unicodedata), so the screen sees normalised text.

families.name: LIVE_EVENT_INSTRUCTION_RE (line 16)
families.purpose: Flag live-event crowd instructions in transcript text so they are excluded from doctrine clips.
hazards: Deciding whether a sentence is a live-event instruction is semantic. Regex cannot separate an instruction from a teaching that mentions the same words (hypothesis: body not read in this sweep).
Ingest-only; should be a reviewed offline label set, not a serve-time gate.

families.name: _MENTION_PATTERNS: sadhguru, amma_bhagavan, iskcon (lines 68-72)
families.purpose: Emit mentions:<teacher> tags only; the module docstring says these never set identity.
hazards: Probe: 'Prabhupada wrote about yoga' and 'Krishna Consciousness is a philosophy' match. This is correct only if the mention tag is never read as identity. Verified from the docstring; the identity-path call sites were not traced here.

families.name: Refusal-phrase patterns (lines 49-53)
families.purpose: Detect assistant refusal or meta phrases in generated text.
hazards: 'i cannot provide (that|this) (information|content)' misses 'i cannot provide the information' (hypothesis, not probed).
Output-side lexicon: misses are safe only if the caller treats no-match as unverified, not as clean.

families.name: Personal-fact extractors (lines 43-45 and nearby)
families.purpose: Extract personal facts such as location and occupation from user text for memory writes.
hazards: 'i live in' and 'i work' patterns misfire on hypotheticals and third-party statements ('my friend lives in Pune' is not matched because of the subject list; 'i work out daily' matches 'i work'). Hypothesis, not probed.
Writes personal data to memory; consent gate lives elsewhere.

families.name: Alias patterns (lines 83, 181, 261-302, 443) and _CLEAN_PREFIX_RE
families.purpose: Map teacher aliases to canonical teacher names and strip title prefixes.
hazards: Hardcoded alias regexes (lines 261-302) duplicate data that also lives in gurus.yaml (the comment at teacher_attribution.py:62-63 says aliases come from gurus.yaml). Hypothesis, not diffed.
Aliases compiled with re.I and \b, so short aliases can match inside other words (hypothesis).

families.name: _SPECIFIC_LOCAL_PATTERNS, _INTERROGATIVE_LOCAL_PATTERNS, _GLOBAL_ROUTING_PATTERNS (lines 163-178)
families.purpose: Choose LightRAG local vs global retrieval mode from the query wording.
hazards: Query-mode routing by regex is a semantic decision; misroutes are silent (hypothesis: not probed).
Entity pattern at line 1005 uses a capitalised bracket form that LLM output may not produce.

families.name: _VIDEO_ID_RE, _TRAILING_ATTR_RE, _LEADING_BOILERPLATE_RE, _TRUNCATED_QUOTE_END_RE (lines 42, 342-373)
families.purpose: Extract video ids; strip extraction boilerplate and truncated-quote tails from OKF entries.
hazards: _TRUNCATED_QUOTE_END_RE is a hardcoded word list (sp|comfo|expre|me|e|t): it can delete real words that end a sentence.
OKF is LLM-extracted (CLAUDE.md invariant 12), so cleanup here cannot make it verbatim.

families.name: _HEADING_RE, _VIDEO_ID_RE (lines 34, 43)
families.purpose: Parse OKF headings and video ids during compile.
hazards: _VIDEO_ID_RE duplicates okf_store (identical).

families.name: _TOKEN_RE, _APOSTROPHE_RE, _QUOTED_STRING_RE (lines 47-50)
families.purpose: Tokenise and normalise apostrophes for exact-substring quote checks, and extract quoted spans.
hazards: Apostrophe normalisation must match the one used for stored text, or the exact-substring check fails closed (correct direction).
_QUOTED_STRING_RE requires 20-400 chars inside quotes, so short verbatim quotes are not extracted.

families.name: _MARKER_RE, _QUOTE_RE (lines 34, 209)
families.purpose: Parse citation markers and quoted spans for citation checks.
hazards: _MARKER_RE overlaps humanizer._CITE_RE (near-duplicate marker grammar).

families.name: _CITE_RE (line 32)
families.purpose: Strip citation markers from output text before display.
hazards: Near-duplicate of citation_service._MARKER_RE with a different accepted syntax (\[\^?\d{1,3}\] vs \[\^(\d{1,3})\]). Two grammars can disagree.

families.name: _ARTIFACT_RE (text_quality_filter.py:101, 408), _LEAKAGE_RE and _MATCH_NOISE_RE (okf_quality_filter.py:39, 44)
families.purpose: Reject extraction artifacts (RAPTOR headers, prompt commentary, leakage) from ingest and OKF text.
hazards: Built with "|".join of pattern lists: one malformed alternative breaks the whole compiled pattern at import time (fails loud, acceptable).
Pattern bodies were not read in this sweep (hypothesis on coverage).

families.name: _WORD_OR_SYM_TOKEN_RE (doctrine_terms.py:298), dynamic \b re.escape(term)\b compile (doctrine_terms.py:429, 436), _TOKEN_RE (doctrine_lexicon.py:56)
families.purpose: Canonicalise doctrine terms and tokenise for lexicon matching.
hazards: \b around terms whose edges are non-word characters (e.g. symbols) never matches, so those terms need a different boundary (hypothesis, not probed).
Dynamic compile per rule: fine at ingest scale; cache if moved to serve.

families.name: _IN_WORD_SUBSTITUTE, _SPACED_LETTERS (lines 47, 50)
families.purpose: Repair in-word substitutions and collapse spaced-out letters (e.g. 'h e l l o').
hazards: _SPACED_LETTERS is ASCII-only [a-z] so it does not repair other scripts (hypothesis, not probed).
Collapsing spaced letters can merge real short words in spaced text.

families.name: _HINDI_PATTERN, _TAMIL_PATTERN (lines 179, 203)
families.purpose: Unicode script-range detection for Hindi and Tamil.
hazards: Script ranges detect script, not language: Marathi and Nepali use Devanagari and would match the Hindi pattern (hypothesis, not probed).

families.file: backend/evaluation/* and backend/benchmarks/* (bench.py 14, abstention_eval.py 12, seeker_relevance_run.py 13, ragas_eval.py, llm_judge.py, verbatim_metrics.py, run_golden_eval.py and others)
families.name: Eval and benchmark pattern sets (grouped)
families.purpose: Parse eval outputs, extract claims and verdicts, score relevance and abstention.
hazards: Eval scorers that use regex to parse LLM judge output inherit the llm_verdict fragility (hypothesis: bodies not read).
Not used at serve time per the file headers; excluded from any latency or safety claim.

families.file: backend/scripts/ops/* and scripts/ops/* (about 45 files), scripts/ingestion/*, scripts/i18n_*, scripts/translate_locales.py, scripts/build_exact_*.py
families.name: Offline ops, ingestion and locale scripts (grouped)
families.purpose: Parse transcripts, subtitles, JSON dumps, locale keys and reports.
hazards: Byte-identical duplicates exist under backend/scripts/ops and scripts/ops (CLAUDE.md invariant). Count these as one family.
Not read individually in this sweep.

families.file: scripts/guards/* (lesson_guards.py 11, pipeline_order_guard.py 10, migration_lint.py 3, stale_flags.py, supabase_types_lint.py 4, guru_literal_guard.py, check_regex_safety.py)
families.name: Guard scripts (grouped)
families.purpose: Enforce pipeline order, migration lint, stale flags and literal guards in pre-commit and CI.
hazards: Guard regexes that read source code are brittle to formatting changes (hypothesis, not probed).
scripts/security/check_regex_safety.py exists, so a ReDoS checker is already in the tree; not run in this sweep.

worst_offenders: backend/rag/intent_prerouter.py:34 DISTRESS_RE: misses 'suicidal' and 'panic attacks' and is reached via preroute_intent, which returns CASUAL for 'hi I am suicidal'. Confirmed by probe. Already registered as A12.
backend/rag/intent_prerouter.py:27 GREETINGS_RE: trailing (\s+.*)? lets 'hi there suicide' match. Safe only because DISTRESS_RE is checked first in preroute_intent (line 95).
backend/app/security_utils.py:37 and :43: $ accepts a trailing newline. _ISO_DATE_RE and _EMAIL_RE return True for values with '\n' appended. Confirmed by probe.
backend/services/pii_scanner.py:10 and backend/app/telemetry_db.py:209: AADHAAR/ID patterns match any grouped 12-digit number, so ids are over-redacted. Confirmed by probe.
backend/app/intake/short_circuit.py:36-124: second greeting grammar with a different vocative list. CLAUDE.md marks it dormant; the caller grep was not run, so this is unconfirmed.
notes: Scope: 249 non-test Python files under backend/ and scripts/ that call re.*, minus the excluded shards. About 40 files were read or probed directly. The rest are grouped by family from grep output and are marked tested=none or hypothesis where bodies were not read. Verified by running patterns: prerouter/DISTRESS_RE false negatives (hi I am suicidal -> CASUAL; I am feeling suicidal -> no match; I have panic attacks -> None); GREETINGS_RE trailing-text match; is_deterministic_greeting correct on 'namaste suicide', 'hi kms', 'hello there', 'Namaste! Good morning.'; $-newline acceptance in _EMAIL_RE and _ISO_DATE_RE; AADHAAR over-match; SSN correct; MEDITATION_RE correct on 'start meditation' and 'what is soul sync'; teacher mention patterns match plain text (mention-only by docstring). Registry: A12 (docs/plans/PROD_READINESS_TASK_LIST_2026-10-11.md) covers the crisis regex non-convergence; the prerouter DISTRESS_RE findings fall under it. No other regex finding was found in docs/analysis/OUTSTANDING_ISSUES.md or the task list by grep for regex/pattern terms, so the remaining findings are recorded as new. The rag/nodes/intent.py:525 call site is live on the graph path but sits behind the Distress stage; the actual user-facing effect of the prerouter false negatives was not traced end to end (hypothesis). No files were edited and no git, docker or data-store writes were made."
false_positive_or_negative_examples: 'hi I am suicidal' | rag/intent_prerouter.py preroute_intent via DISTRESS_RE | got CASUAL | expected DISTRESS (false negative)
'I am feeling suicidal' | rag/intent_prerouter.py DISTRESS_RE | got no match | expected match (false negative; no stemming)
'I have panic attacks' | rag/intent_prerouter.py DISTRESS_RE via preroute_intent | got None | expected DISTRESS (false negative; \battack\b rejects 'attacks')
'hi there suicide' | rag/intent_prerouter.py GREETINGS_RE | got match (CASUAL when called alone) | expected no match (false positive; masked only by DISTRESS-first ordering)
'a@b.co\n' | backend/app/security_utils.py _EMAIL_RE | got True | expected False (false positive; $ accepts trailing newline)
'2026-11-15T10:00:00+05:30\n' | backend/app/security_utils.py _ISO_DATE_RE | got True | expected False (false positive; $ accepts trailing newline)
'ref 1234 5678 9012' | backend/services/pii_scanner.py AADHAAR_REGEX (also app/telemetry_db.py ID_REGEX) | got match (redacted) | expected no match (false positive; over-redaction of reference ids)
'000-12-3456' | backend/services/pii_scanner.py SSN_REGEX | got no match | expected no match (correct; included as a control for SSN)
